Humphreys (R158 p.532): 'Communication with all points of it had been made easy by removing such of the fences as were in the way' (limited Union removal on his front). NOT in the OR: the 836-holes rail, Klingle/Sherfy fence losses by July 4, post-and-rail on both sides of the Emmitsburg Road, Jul 3 delay of Pickett's Charge.
tier_suggestion: documented (fences impeded the advance; some removed by Humphreys); breach points and fence types open

passage: Before the army left Gettysburg, and knowing that the wounded had been brought in from the field, six ambulances and four wagons were ordered to be left from each corps, to convey the wounded from their hospitals to the railroad depot, for. transportation to the other hospitals. From the Cavalry Corps but four ambulances were ordered
note: Counts (6 ambulances + 4 wagons per corps; Cavalry Corps 4 ambulances) supported, but this is a post-battle arrangement made before the army left Gettysburg (about Jul 4-5), not a Jul 2 afternoon fact. Four-wheel spring ambulance, driver and two stretcher-bearers, and Taneytown Road/Baltimore Pike routes are not in the passage.
tier_suggestion: documented (post-battle allotment); Jul 2 role and routes inferred

passage: These regiments were withdrawn about 3 p. m., and, by order of General Gregg, I threw forward the Tenth New York Cavalry, under command of Major Avery, and deployed skirmishers to occupy the ground vacated.
note: J. I. Gregg: brigade took position on the Hanover pike about 2 miles from Gettysburg about 11 a. m. Jul 2; after the infantry skirmishers were withdrawn about 3 p. m. the 10th New York Cavalry skirmishers were deployed; at 6 o'clock 50 dismounted men were driven back. 'Brinkerhoff Ridge' is not OR wording; Rank's section of Battery H, 3rd Pa. Heavy Artillery is not named for Jul 2 at this location, so that sub-claim stays open.
tier_suggestion: documented (10th NY skirmishers about 15:00 on the Hanover pike); Brinkerhoff Ridge and Rank's guns open

passage: Along this wall the division was then formed, Semmes in reserve to me and Barksdale on my left, supported by Wofford, in reserve.
note: About 3 p. m. the head of Kershaw's column came into the open field and formed line behind a stone wall: Kershaw and Barksdale in line, Semmes and Wofford in reserve (two forward, two reserve). 'Parallel to the Emmitsburg Road' is implied (skirmishers 'extending along the Emmitsburg road'), not stated; 'Millerstown Road, Warfield Ridge' are not named in the passage (Kershaw mentions the cross-road/schoolhouse road).
tier_suggestion: documented (disposition about 15:00); place names inferred

passage: I have to-day, up to this hour, awaited the attack of the enemy, I having a strong position for defensive.
note: Meade to Halleck, July 2, 3 p. m. (rec'd July 3): telegram supported. NOT in the OR text read: Sickles asking to be excused from Meade's meeting, Warren reporting the III Corps misplaced, and the hour of Meade's rebuke (gap). The council minutes (p.73) are a later meeting.
tier_suggestion: documented (3 p.m. telegram); Sickles/Warren items open

passage: when the enemy opened on him with several batteries in his front and on his flank, and immediately brought forward columns of infantry and made a most vigorous assault.
note: Meade: while explaining to Sickles that he was too far in advance, the enemy opened with several batteries (no hour). Clark (R182 p.586): 'about 3 p. m. ... a rebel battery ... opened fire on my position'. 'Union artillery opens on Longstreet's arriving divisions' is Clark's earlier (about 2 p. m., p.585) fire, not an opening at 15:00.
tier_suggestion: documented (Confederate batteries open about 15:00); Union first fire at about 14:00 per Clark
